findings.title: U1 pin EN is floating / undriven
findings.failure_mode: A floating EN/CHIP_PU leaves the module in an indeterminate reset state — unreliable or no boot.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet + hardware design guidelines: EN (CHIP_PU) must be pulled up (typ. 10k) with a delay cap; it must not float or the module may not boot reliably.

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 100n
findings.failure_mode: A 1uF (instead of 100nF) cap on IO0 defeats the auto-download/reset sequence — can't flash without manual BOOT.
findings.citation: ESP32 auto-program circuit: IO0 uses a 100nF cap. A 1uF cap here (as on EN) is too large and breaks the auto-download timing.

findings.title: Pin not connected
Pin not connected
Board has malformed outline (no edges found on Edge.Cuts layer)
DevKit 3V3 pins tied via R31 (0Ω) to board +3.3V rail while 5V pin is also powered
findings.detail: U1's 5V pin is driven from +5V, so the DevKit's onboard LDO produces 3.3V on its 3V3 header pins. Those pins go through R31 (0Ω) onto +3.3V, which U16 (AP2112K-3.3) also drives. The datasheet says the 5V and 3V3 power inputs are mutually exclusive. As built, two LDO outputs are paralleled, and when USB is plugged in, the DevKit's regulator can back-feed the whole +3.3V rail. Choose one approach: leave R31 unpopulated and let the DevKit power itself from 5V, or power the module from 3V3 alone and leave its 5V pin unconnected.
findings.failure_mode: The two regulators fight each other, and current can flow backwards into one of them. Load sharing between them is uncontrolled. When USB is plugged in, the DevKit's LDO may end up powering the DAC, display and op-amp loads on +3.3V.

findings.title: U15 channel B (pins 5,6,7) not present in netlist – unused amplifier unterminated
findings.detail: The netlist contains only pins 1–4 and 8 of U15; the second amplifier (VIN2+ pin 5, VIN2- pin 6, VO2 pin 7) is not placed or connected, so on the PCB these pads will be left floating. Unused op-amp channels should be configured as a follower with the + input tied to a defined voltage (e.g. GND).
findings.failure_mode: Floating FET inputs on channel B can make it oscillate or rail, which adds supply current, heating and crosstalk into the CENTER_BIAS buffer on channel A.
findings.excerpt: VIN2+ 5 I Amplifier 2 noninverting input pin

findings.title: U8 VREF driven by ±12V op-amp can reach the ±12V absolute-max limit
findings.detail: U8's VREF pin (pin 7) is driven directly by U4B's output. U4 is an OPA2810 powered from +12V and -12V, and its rail-to-rail output can swing to roughly ±11.8V. The two stages in front of it (U4A with a gain of about 5 set by R6/R5, and U4B with a gain of about 4 set by R10/R9) give a high overall gain. Any DC offset, clipping or large input will push VREF to within a few hundred millivolts of the ±12V absolute-max rating, and transients during power sequencing could go past it. Confirm the worst-case VREF swing, or add clamping or reduce the gain so there is margin.
findings.failure_mode: If the op-amp rails or overshoot take VREF beyond ±12V, the DAC's R-2R ladder input can be damaged.
findings.excerpt: VREF, RFB to GND −12 V to +12 V

findings.title: ILI9341 module datasheet unavailable; DS1 not audited against a datasheet
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for DS1 (ILI9341 14-pin SPI TFT module with touch). Its pins couldn't be checked against a datasheet. Two things need a manual check: the LED backlight pin is driven directly by ESP32 GPIO17, so the module's backlight current must be within what the GPIO can supply; and T_DOUT (GPIO6) and SDO (no-connect) share the SPI bus with the display, which is fine only if the touch controller tri-states its output when T_CS is high.
findings.failure_mode: Errors that need the datasheet to spot, such as backlight current exceeding the GPIO limit or a missing series resistor, could go unnoticed.

findings.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 not verified
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for SW3 (TS5A23157), so I could not check its pinout, supply range or decoupling against the manufacturer's specifications. It uses a module footprint (ohmen:TS5A23157_Module), so the pin mapping also needs to be checked against the module.
findings.failure_mode: If the module pinout doesn't match the symbol, the AD9833 outputs could be routed to the wrong channel or the switch could get no power.

findings.title: U1 pin EN has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing EN pull-up => no defined power-on reset delay.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: EN uses a ~10k pull-up to 3V3 plus a 1uF delay cap (RC reset).

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing IO0 pull-up can leave the module entering download mode unexpectedly.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: IO0 (boot strap) needs a pull-up (typ. 10k) so the module boots to flash by default.

dropped.title: DevKit fed on both 5V and 3V3 pins; its onboard LDO output is paralleled with U16 through R31 (0 Ω)
dropped.detail: U1 pin 21 (5V) sits on +5V (LM7805 U3 output and AP2112 U16 input). U1 pins 1 and 2 (3V3) go through R31 (0 Ω) to the board's +3.3V rail, which U16 drives. The DevKit has its own 3.3 V LDO powered from its 5V pin, so its 3V3 pins are a regulator output. That puts the DevKit LDO and U16 directly in parallel. The datasheet says the 5V pin and the 3V3 pin are mutually exclusive ways to power the board. Also, when USB is plugged in, the DevKit's USB 5 V is tied to the 5V pin and drives back into the LM7805 output.
dropped.failure_mode: Two LDOs on one rail fight each other and share current unpredictably, so one of them may end up carrying the whole load. With USB connected while the board is powered (for example during programming), USB 5 V and the 7805 output are tied together and can backfeed the host or the regulator. Fix: leave R31 unpopulated and let each side regulate its own 3.3 V, or power the DevKit through only one pin.

dropped.title: ILI9341 module datasheet not available; DS1 not verified
dropped.detail: No datasheet could be found for DS1 (an ILI9341 TFT module with a touch controller), so its pin connections could not be checked against the manufacturer's specifications. In the netlist, VCC is on +3.3V. The display and touch controller share SCK and MOSI on GPIO4 and GPIO5, with separate chip selects on GPIO7 and GPIO18. The backlight pin LED is driven directly by GPIO17. SDO(MISO) is left unconnected.
dropped.failure_mode: Without the module datasheet, nobody can confirm that 3.3 V VCC is correct for this module. Nobody can confirm either that GPIO17 can drive the LED pin directly without a transistor on the module.
